name: Writing Checklist
description: A writing checklist that walks the writing process from planning to final proofread.

items.text: Reread the prompt and note the exact requirements.
Confirm the length, format and citation style needed.
Brainstorm ideas and gather your sources or evidence.
Write a clear thesis or main argument in one sentence.
Outline your main points and the order to make them.
Note the evidence or examples supporting each point.
Follow your outline and write without stopping to perfect it.
items.note: Get ideas down first; polish comes later.

items.text: Open with an introduction that states your thesis.
Give each paragraph one clear main idea.
Support each point with evidence and your own analysis.
Write a conclusion that ties the argument together.
Leave placeholders for anything you need to look up.
Check the draft actually answers the prompt.
Confirm every paragraph supports your thesis.
Reorder paragraphs so the argument flows logically.
Add evidence where claims are thin and cut what is off-topic.
Strengthen transitions between paragraphs and ideas.
Tighten wordy sentences and remove repetition.
Replace vague words with precise ones.
Vary sentence length so the writing reads smoothly.
Check the tone matches the assignment.
Make sure each sentence is clear on a first read.
Take a break, then read the whole thing aloud.
Fix spelling, grammar and punctuation errors.
Check citations and the reference list are complete and correct.
Confirm formatting, font, spacing and the title page.
Verify your name, the word count and the file name.
Submit on time and confirm the upload went through.

faq.q: What are the stages of the writing process?
faq.a: The writing process has five stages: planning your argument and outline, drafting without over-editing, revising the structure and content, editing sentences and word choice, and proofreading for spelling, grammar and formatting before you submit.

faq.q: What is the difference between revising and editing?
faq.a: Revising works on big-picture issues like argument, structure, evidence and clarity of ideas. Editing then fixes sentence-level problems such as wording, flow and concision. Revise first, because there is no point polishing sentences you may cut.

faq.q: How do I start writing an essay?
faq.a: Start by understanding the prompt, then build a clear thesis and an outline of your main points with supporting evidence. Planning before you draft gives the essay direction and saves you from rewriting later.

faq.q: How can I proofread my own work effectively?
faq.a: Take a break before proofreading, read the text aloud or backward sentence by sentence, check one issue at a time, and verify formatting and citations. A fresh pair of eyes or a read-aloud tool catches errors you skim past.

faq.q: Can I download this writing checklist as a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. You can print it to keep beside your laptop or download it as a PDF to your phone and follow the same process for every assignment.
